proposed_widenings.name: DamageTypeRef.wielded_weapon_type
proposed_widenings.justification: The extra 2d6 damage is 'of the weapon's type' — it mirrors whatever damage type the wielded weapon deals. This is neither a fixed DamageType nor a CastTimeChoice<DamageType>. A new variant { kind: 'wielded_weapon_type' } is needed so the damage atom can defer the type to the wielded weapon's profile at resolution time.
proposed_widenings.evidence: the Giant takes an extra 2d6 damage of the weapon's type

proposed_widenings.name: MasteryTrigger.typeFilter (creature type filter on on-hit trigger)
proposed_widenings.justification: The on-hit rider fires only when the target is a Giant. OnHitTriggerMechanics / MasteryTrigger has no typeFilter field to narrow the trigger to one or more CreatureType values. Without it the trigger cannot be scoped to Giants; any encoding omitting the filter would fire against all targets, which is incorrect.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When you hit a Giant with this weapon

proposed_widenings.name: MagicItemOnHitEffect: composite damage + save_gate
proposed_widenings.justification: The on-hit effect is a two-part outcome: (a) 2d6 damage and (b) a DC 15 Str save-or-Prone. MasteryEffect only supports SaveGateRider | ModifyRollAdvantageRider | GrantWeaponAttackRider. SaveGateRider.onFail is SaveGateRiderResult (apply_condition | none) and cannot include a separate damage instance. There is no way to express 'damage plus save_gate' as a single MasteryEffect. A composite on-hit effect shape (e.g., a new variant that wraps ReadonlyNonEmptyArray<MasteryEffect>, or widening SaveGateRider to optionally include a pre-save damage atom) is needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: the Giant takes an extra 2d6 damage of the weapon's type and must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or have the Prone condition

notes: The passive +1 to attack rolls and damage rolls (Mechanic 1) fits cleanly as PassiveMechanics with modify_roll_numeric and modify_damage_numeric both scoped via weaponFilter: specific_item. The on-hit rider (Mechanic 2) requires three surface widenings and cannot be honestly encoded without them. No dhall/json/trace files are produced.
